applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Convention between France and the People's Republic of China for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, signed 26 November 2013

Convention between France and the United States for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income and Capital, signed 31 August 1994, as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Primary provisions are Code monétaire et financier Articles L.561-2, L.561-2-2, L.561-4-1, L.561-5, L.561-5-1, L.561-6, L.561-10, L.561-15, L.561-32 and L.561-46 to L.561-50; implementing provisions include Articles R.561-1 to R.561-22. The beneficial-owner filing is maintained through the Registre national des entreprises under Code de commerce Articles L.561-46 to L.561-50 and related regulatory provisions. The French AML framework implements EU Directive (EU) 2015/849, as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843 and subsequent EU measures. A beneficial owner is generally an individual owning, directly or indirectly, more than 25% of capital or voting rights, or exercising control by other means; if no individual is identifiable after reasonable investigation, the relevant legal representative or equivalent senior managing official is recorded in accordance with applicable law.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before incorporation, onboarding, banking and each material transaction, screen all UBOs, directors, authorized signatories, shareholders, counterparties, banks, vessels and key intermediaries against United Nations Security Council lists, European Union sanctions regulations and consolidated EU financial-sanctions data, French national measures, OFAC SDN and other relevant OFAC lists, and commercially maintained PEP, relatives-and-close-associates and adverse-media databases. Apply a documented risk-based procedure under the Code monétaire et financier, including identity resolution, beneficial-ownership verification, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth review, sanctions false-positive adjudication, senior-management approval for PEP relationships, enhanced monitoring, suspicious-transaction escalation to TRACFIN where required, and prohibition of dealings with designated persons or entities. OFAC screening is mandatory where there is a US nexus, US person, US financial institution, US goods or services, or other applicable jurisdictional connection; EU and French measures apply independently of OFAC.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises operated by the Institut national de la propriété industrielle (INPI): https://formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; the Registre national des entreprises is maintained by INPI
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered corporate name must be stated in the incorporation documents and filing in a form compatible with French legal and registry requirements. Latin characters and French orthographic conventions are ordinarily accepted. A foreign-language or transliterated name may be used if it is not misleading, unlawful, confusingly similar to an existing protected sign or corporate name, or contrary to public order. The SAS designation must appear in the constitutional documents and the legal form must be disclosed in the corporate name or accompanying legal-form indication as required by French company law. Name availability does not establish trademark availability; a separate search of the Registre national des entreprises, INPI trademark databases, EUIPO records, domain names and relevant trade names is required.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms suggesting a regulated financial, banking, insurance, payment, investment-services, credit, lending or asset-management activity without the required authorization
Terms falsely implying a public authority, ministry, embassy, court, municipality, sovereign body or official governmental status
Terms protected by statute or requiring approval, including references to regulated professions, public institutions, universities or legally protected designations where applicable
Words or expressions contrary to law, public order or morality
Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing company, trademark, trade name or protected sign
Geographical, national or international institutional references that create a misleading impression of official affiliation
Names implying a business activity materially different from the declared corporate purpose or requiring a license not held by the company
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not generally provide a separate statutory company-name reservation certificate with a universal 30-day legal validity period. The 30-day period is an operational planning window for a provisional name hold or filing workflow and must be confirmed with the selected filing professional. Conduct registry, INPI trademark, EUIPO, domain and trade-name searches before filing. If the Guichet unique or registry rejects the name, obtain the written deficiency or rejection notice, identify whether the issue concerns similarity, prohibited terminology, legal-form wording, public order or incomplete evidence, and submit a corrected filing or administrative response through the Guichet unique within the prescribed deadline. Where the decision is an appealable administrative decision, seek reconsideration from the competent authority and, if necessary, lodge an administrative appeal before the competent administrative court within the applicable deadline, ordinarily two months from notification unless the notice states otherwise. A revised name is usually faster and lower risk than litigation. Trademark objections must be addressed separately through INPI opposition or court procedures, as applicable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A French SAS must have a registered office in France under the Code de commerce. Domiciliation at an approved domiciliation company is generally permissible under Code de commerce Articles L.123-11-1 et seq., subject to an eligible contract, disclosure of the registered office, access to company records and compliance with the domiciliation provider's regulatory obligations. A director's personal residence may be used subject to statutory conditions and duration limits. For an offshore trade intermediary and commercial re-invoicing hub, a virtual office is legally possible but presents elevated banking, VAT, customs, transfer-pricing, permanent-establishment, economic-substance and AML risk. The company should maintain accessible books and records, genuine management activity, documented contracting and invoicing functions, local accounting and tax support, operational evidence, transaction files, counterparties' due diligence and a commercially credible reason for the French location.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No official national percentage is published. For this medium-risk enhanced AML business model, an estimated 10% to 20% annual probability of an unannounced or short-notice physical verification or equivalent documentary inspection is a planning estimate, not a statutory statistic. The risk may materially increase where the company uses a virtual office, has non-resident directors, reports limited French activity, handles high-value cross-border goods, claims VAT positions, has customs exposure, receives AML alerts or presents inconsistencies between registered activity and actual operations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce): Articles L.227-1 to L.227-30 (SAS), L.210-1 to L.210-10 (general incorporation rules); Décret n° 2021-300 creating the Guichet Unique; R.227-1 and R.227-2 (registration formalities)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court) via the INPI electronic Guichet Unique for Enterprises at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration de constitution de la société (dossier M0 / immatriculation DPO) accompanied by the Statuts (Articles of Association), the attestation de dépôt des fonds and the pouvoir de représentation, filed electronically through the Guichet Unique
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum share capital (may be as low as EUR 1); however, for cash contributions at least 50% of the par value must be paid up at incorporation (Art. L.227-2) and the balance within 5 years. Funds are placed in a blocked escrow-type account in the name of the 'société en formation' with a French bank or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, and are released only upon presentation of the Kbis registration certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION ONE — Share subscription. All shareholders unanimously subscribe one hundred ordinary shares and release at least fifty per cent of their par value per Article L.227-2 of the Commercial Code. RESOLUTION TWO — Registered office. The shareholders adopt the registered office set out in Article 4 of the Statuts and authorise the President to complete all registry and tax filings for that address. RESOLUTION THREE — Officer appointment. The shareholders appoint [Given Name] [Surname] as President of the SAS, with full corporate powers. RESOLUTION FOUR — Powers. The President receives delegation to open bank accounts, sign commercial contracts, and execute incorporation formalities before the Greffe and the INPI Guichet Unique.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, execute and optionally notarise the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: All shareholders acting as constitutive assembly; legal counsel or a notaire (avocat) drafting the Statuts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SAS Statuts comprising the corporate name, registered office address, corporate object (wholesale re-invoicing trade, ISIC 4690), share capital, share transfer restrictions and the inaugural President. Each shareholder signs the Statuts or a collegiate resolution per Article L.227-5. For cash shares, state the amount released and the payment schedule; for in-kind contributions, obtain a commissaire aux apports valuation report. Finalise the beneficial owner declaration (RBE) for submission at registration.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or identity document of each shareholder
Draft Statuts (Articles of Association)
Appointment of the President and corporate governance structure
Entity chart and certificate of good standing where a shareholder is a legal person
Beneficial owners declaration (Déclaration du bénéficiaire effectif)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Statuts or supporting documents are queried for missing clauses, invalid share transfer lock or corporate-object wording, prepare an addendum deed (acte modificatif), re-sign it before all shareholders and submit the corrective dossier via the Guichet Unique within the registry's 15-day cure window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open a blocked capital deposit account and release the share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution authorised by the ACPR, or the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations as fallback escrow agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the signed Statuts and the President's identification to the bank and open an account in the name 'Société en formation — [Name] SAS'. Deposit at least 50% of the par value of the cash shares. The bank issues the attestation de dépôt des fonds (capital deposit certificate) listing the amount held. The funds remain blocked until the Kbis is issued; the certificate must be attached to the M0 incorporation file.
required_dossiers: Signed Statuts
Identity documents of the President and shareholders
Bank KYC forms including final beneficial owner declaration
Proof of address and supporting economic substance for non-resident shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening (KYC rejection or incomplete RBE), approach a second established French bank or deposit with the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations; correct the beneficial ownership documentation before referral to the ACPR mediation desk if access issues persist.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the constitution notice in an accredited legal announcements newspaper (JAL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Accredited Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) published in the department of the registered office (e.g., Les Echos or Petites Affiches for Paris)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notice to the JAL containing the company name, legal form (SAS), share capital, registered office, corporate object (ISIC 4690 wholesale trade and re-invoicing), duration, share transfer restrictions and the President's identity. Upon payment, the JAL issues the attestation de parution which must bear a date not older than three months at the date of registry filing. Attach the certificate to the M0 file.
required_dossiers: Attestation de dépôt des fonds (capital deposit certificate)
Signed Statuts
Identity details of the President and management powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the JAL refuses publication due to content mismatch or unpaid fees, correct the wording and republish in another accredited JAL of the same department; if the Greffe requires a more recent publication, request a new dated attestation from the original JAL.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Dematerialised filing of the incorporation file on the Guichet Unique (INPI)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Guichet Unique électronique des formalités d'entreprises operated by the INPI, with substantive examination by the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce for RCS registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open an account at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr, complete the M0 declaration, upload the scanned Statuts, the attestation de parution, the capital deposit certificate, the identity documents, the RBE declaration, the bulletin n°2 (non-condemnation) of the President and the proof of jouissance of the registered office. Sign electronically, pay the registration fee by bank card or wire transfer, and monitor the dossier status until the Greffe delivers the Kbis.
required_dossiers: M0 declaration (electronically prefilled by the portal)
Statuts dated and signed in original scanned form
Attestation de parution du JAL
Attestation de dépôt des fonds
Beneficial owners declaration (RBE)
Proof of jouissance of the registered office (lease or domiciliation agreement)
Bulletin n°2 — non-condemnation certificate of the President
Identity documents of all shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Greffe clerk or INPI issues observations within 5 working days, complete the missing attachments, amend the Statuts or correct the RBE via the Guichet Unique account within the maximum 15-day curative delay; after 15 days of inactivity, resubmit a fresh application to reactivate the registration process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration opening: Kbis delivery, corporate governance books and tax/social enrolments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Kbis), DGFIP (SIRET and VAT number), URSSAF (social security affiliation) and CCI (professional trading registration)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After registration, collect the Kbis extract from the RCS; the SIREN/SIRET number is automatically transmitted to DGFIP and URSSAF. Open the definitive operational bank account and release the escrowed capital upon presentation of the Kbis. Set up the corporate registers (registre des décisions, registre des mouvements de titres), enrol with URSSAF, obtain the French VAT number through the DGFIP electronic service, and verify the RBE registration with the Registre National des Entreprises. No separate trading license is required for the pure re-invoicing wholesale activity.
required_dossiers: Kbis extract issued by the Greffe
Capital deposit certificate for release of escrowed funds
Final bank account opening forms
URSSAF activity declaration and affiliation forms
Power of attorney of the President for tax representation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis contains inaccurate SIRET, officers or corporate-object data, file a rectification request with the Greffe via the Guichet Unique; if a bank refuses the final account, provide the Kbis and corrected INSEE documentation, or escalate to the ACPR banking-access mediation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 4690 pure commercial re-invoicing and offshore trade intermediary involves no physical manufacturing; the reference authorities remain the Direction Générale des Entreprises (DGE / Ministry of Economy and Finance) and the Chambre de Commerce et d'Industrie (CCI Paris Île-de-France) for commercial registrations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés — Extrait Kbis (automatic trading-premises clearance); no specific industrial or operational permit is required for general wholesale re-invoicing trade

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de la Transition Écologique / DREAL (Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement) — competent only if physical premises are added
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the pure commercial intermediary does not reach any ICPE (Installation classée pour la Protection de l'Environnement) threshold; administrative registration would arise only if the company later adds a warehouse or logistics facility exceeding declared capacity limits (Code de l'environnement, Art. L.511-1)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: None applicable at incorporation for re-invoicing trade; if later adding storage facilities, comply with the ICPE regime and the limit values of Arrêté du 2 février 1998 (15 mg/l suspended solids, 50 mg/l BOD5) and the VOC emission thresholds of Directive 2010/75/EU transposed in Articles R.515-58 et seq. of the Environmental Code

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate for the leased offices (attestation ERP Type X for premises open to the public, or simple declaration of mixed-occupancy building per Article R.123-22 of the Construction and Housing Code); structural load inspection evidenced by the landlord's ERP/ERPS conformity certificate; occupational clearance: registration of premises with CARSAT (Risques Professionnels), preparation of the Document Unique d'Évaluation des Risques Professionnels (DUERP) before first hiring, electrical installation verification per Articles R.4214-1 to R.4214-18 of the Labour Code, and compliance with workplace health and safety standards of Code du travail Article L.4121-1.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via official portal impots.gouv.fr
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: French SAS entities register with INSEE to obtain SIREN/SIRET number serving as statutory TIN; VAT identification number (TVA) is automatically assigned upon registration. Foreign-owned entities follow identical incorporation and tax authority registration procedures.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections; hybrid mismatch rules apply under Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD)

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 77,700 EUR (mandatory registration if prior-year turnover exceeded)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory facturation électronique for B2B transactions with real-time data transmission to tax authorities and digital stamping

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate on exports of goods to non-EU countries or territories upon proof of export; offshore services subject to specific conditions
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties up to 40% of evaded VAT plus interest; retrospective clawback of benefits and potential criminal prosecution for fraudulent claims

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, acting within the Eurosystem under the European Central Bank framework; foreign-exchange, customs and statistical reporting also involve the French customs authority, Direction générale des douanes et droits indirects, and the European Central Bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France uses the euro and has no general exchange controls. Current-account transactions, including imports, exports, services, dividends, interest, royalties and ordinary profit remittances, are generally freely convertible and transferable through regulated financial institutions. Capital-account transactions are also generally unrestricted, subject to EU and French foreign-investment screening, sanctions, anti-money-laundering, counter-terrorist-financing, tax, beneficial-ownership and bank-compliance requirements. A French SAS may remit dividends or other distributions only after legally distributable profits are established, statutory accounts are approved, required losses and reserves are addressed, and applicable withholding-tax, treaty-relief and beneficial-owner documentation is satisfied. Interest, royalties, management fees and related-party payments require arm's-length support, transfer-pricing documentation, corporate-benefit evidence, withholding-tax analysis and invoice or agreement support. Payments involving sanctioned jurisdictions, sanctioned persons, restricted goods or unexplained circular flows may be blocked or reported. Cash transactions and certain cross-border payment or statistical reporting obligations may apply depending on amount, instrument, counterparty and transaction type.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France has no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio or general deadline requiring export receipts to be converted into euros. Export proceeds may generally remain in foreign-currency accounts or be converted at the company's discretion. The company must retain commercial, customs, banking and accounting evidence supporting the transaction, accurately record foreign-currency balances and recognize exchange differences under French accounting rules. Cross-border payments may be subject to bank, customs, statistical, sanctions and anti-money-laundering controls. Export declarations and customs evidence must be completed where legally required, and VAT treatment must be supported by appropriate transport and customs documentation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole S.A. and the relevant Crédit Agricole regional bank
BPCE S.A. and the relevant Banque Populaire or Caisse d'Epargne institution

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for operational payments and foreign-currency collections, but insufficient as the sole treasury platform for a re-invoicing hub. A French SAS may use an EU-authorized electronic-money institution or payment institution under passporting rules, subject to the provider's French servicing status, safeguarding model, permitted services, transaction limits and risk appetite. An offshore digital EMI without EU authorization, passporting, or an EU-regulated partner cannot lawfully provide regulated payment-account or payment-execution services to the company merely through an online platform. EMIs generally do not provide bank deposits, capital escrow services, full trade-finance capability or equivalent deposit-guarantee protection. The company should maintain a regulated French or EU bank as its primary account, segregate customer or third-party funds where applicable, and document payment purposes, counterparties, beneficial owners, source of funds and expected transaction corridors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not impose a universal requirement that all directors physically attend a bank branch for account opening. Remote onboarding may be permitted using qualified or reliable electronic identification, certified corporate documents, video verification and beneficial-owner checks. The bank may nevertheless require an in-person meeting or live video interview, particularly for a newly incorporated SAS, non-resident shareholders or directors, complex ownership, high-risk jurisdictions, re-invoicing activity, unusual payment corridors, large expected turnover, or trade-finance requests. The capital escrow account is opened subject to incorporation documents and the bank's acceptance; the blocked capital is released after registration evidence is provided. Remote onboarding is discretionary and not a statutory entitlement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Re-invoicing-hub model with large cross-border flows but limited employees, premises, inventory or operating substance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board-approved business plan; transaction-flow diagram; customer and supplier contracts; invoices and purchase orders; logistics and customs process; evidence of personnel, office, service providers and decision-making in France; expected monthly volumes; gross-margin analysis; and written explanation of the entity's commercial role.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership, nominee shareholders, indirect control, or inability to identify the ultimate beneficial owner.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current articles of association; Kbis extract; cap table; shareholder register; ownership chart to natural persons; passports and proof of address for directors, shareholders and beneficial owners; beneficial-owner declaration; trust or foundation documentation where relevant; and corporate authorization for account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned, high-risk or politically exposed persons, jurisdictions or sectors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC files; sanctions and PEP screening records; certificates of incorporation; licenses or registrations; beneficial-owner confirmations; end-use and end-user statements; transport documents; customs declarations; contractual sanctions clauses; and documented escalation and rejection procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume third-party payments, pass-through transfers, circular funds or payment flows inconsistent with invoices.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-way reconciliation between contracts, invoices, purchase orders, shipping records and bank statements; payment-purpose matrix; approval controls; segregation-of-duties policy; counterparty master-data controls; intercompany settlement policy; and written explanation of any netting, offsets, advances or refunds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign-source capital, shareholder loans or intercompany funding with unclear source of funds or repayment basis.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholder resolutions; subscription or loan agreements; funding-bank statements; audited or management accounts of the funder; tax-residence certificates; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; ultimate-owner documentation; arm's-length interest analysis; and French accounting entries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected turnover, currencies, countries or payment purposes materially differ from the onboarding profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated rolling treasury forecast; variance explanation; revised customer and supplier schedule; management accounts; customs and VAT evidence; board-approved change notification; and documented periodic KYC refresh.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Weak tax and accounting substance, unexplained related-party margins, or suspected VAT carousel or fraud exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer-pricing policy; intercompany agreements; arm's-length benchmarking; VAT registrations and filings; customs records; statutory accounts; tax-residence evidence; beneficial-owner records; internal-control descriptions; and independent accountant or auditor confirmation where available.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route paid-in capital through a regulated French or EU bank to the SAS capital escrow account using an international wire transfer or SEPA transfer where applicable. The payment reference should identify the French SAS, subscriber, share subscription, amount, currency and corporate purpose. Provide the bank with the subscription agreement or capital contribution resolution, identity and beneficial-owner documents of the subscriber, source-of-funds evidence, bank-account ownership evidence and incorporation file. After registration, provide the Kbis extract or equivalent registration evidence so the bank can release the blocked funds to the operational account. Shareholder loans, cash pooling and intercompany funding should be routed under signed agreements with documented terms, transfer-pricing support, tax analysis and a clear purpose code or payment narrative. The bank may request evidence for each material inbound transfer and may delay or reject funds pending sanctions, AML, source-of-funds and beneficial-owner verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SEPA Credit Transfer for eligible euro payments within the SEPA area and SWIFT customer credit transfer, commonly evidenced by an MT103 or its ISO 20022 equivalent, for non-SEPA or non-euro payments. Each payment should identify the contracting party, invoice number, goods or services, purchase-order reference, currency, value date and beneficiary account. Maintain the commercial invoice, purchase order, contract, transport document, customs declaration, import or export evidence, VAT analysis and sanctions screening record. For higher-risk or larger transactions, use an irrevocable documentary commercial letter of credit issued or confirmed by a regulated bank, with defined Incoterms, documentary conditions, inspection requirements, discrepancy controls and insurance provisions. Use bank collection, open-account settlement or supply-chain finance only after counterparty, country, goods, fraud and sanctions risk review. Avoid unexplained third-party beneficiaries, split payments, cash settlement and circular flows. Reconcile all trade payments to the general ledger, customs records and VAT returns.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards with a regulated bank or eligible investment firm, used for identifiable commercial exposures and documented under an ISDA or equivalent master agreement.

Non-deliverable forwards where the relevant currency is restricted or non-deliverable, subject to counterparty authorization, applicable EU and French financial-markets rules, EMIR reporting, collateral and risk-management requirements, and confirmation that the instrument is not used to evade exchange controls.

Currency swaps and cross-currency interest-rate swaps for documented funding or balance-sheet exposures, subject to suitability, counterparty-credit, collateral, valuation, EMIR and accounting controls.
Foreign-exchange spot transactions for ordinary settlement and liquidity management through regulated banks or payment providers.

Currency options or option structures only after assessing product governance, appropriateness, premium, leverage, accounting and corporate-authority requirements; speculative or uncovered positions should be prohibited by treasury policy.

All derivatives should be supported by a written hedging policy, approved limits, authorized counterparties, exposure forecasts, confirmation and reconciliation controls, independent valuation, collateral procedures, ISDA or equivalent documentation, EMIR classification and reporting analysis, and hedge-accounting documentation where applied.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval and filing of annual accounts and management report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders and competent Commercial Court Registry (Greffe du tribunal de commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Accounts must generally be approved within six months after financial year-end and filed within one month after approval, or within two months if filed electronically.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may trigger a court injunction, a civil fine generally up to EUR 1,500, increased to EUR 3,000 for repeat breaches, and registry compliance measures. France has no automatic statutory strike-off solely for late annual-account filing; prolonged inactivity or unresolved non-compliance may support administrative or court-ordered removal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and tax package (Form 2065 and applicable schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Tax Administration (Direction générale des finances publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally by the fifteenth day of the fourth month after financial year-end; for a calendar-year taxpayer, normally by the second business day following 1 May. Electronic filing is mandatory.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing generally attracts a 10% surcharge, late-payment interest generally calculated at 0.20% per month, and potentially increased penalties for deliberate or fraudulent conduct. There is no automatic administrative strike-off for tax-return lateness.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual review of beneficial ownership and filing of amendments where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent Commercial Court Registry through the beneficial ownership register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: France does not impose a separate annual beneficial-owner confirmation filing. Changes in beneficial ownership or control generally must be reported within 30 days; an annual internal verification should be documented.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to disclose or maintain accurate beneficial-owner information may result in criminal penalties, including fines for the company and responsible officers, registry injunctions, and restrictions on registration or business formalities. No automatic annual strike-off applies solely because an annual confirmation is absent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' decision approving accounts and allocating profit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SAS; filing with the Commercial Court Registry occurs through the annual accounts package
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within six months after financial year-end, unless a court grants an extension.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene or document the annual decision may expose the legal representative to liability, injunctions, and difficulties filing annual accounts. No separate automatic administrative strike-off is triggered solely by failure to record the shareholders' decision.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor is generally mandatory when the SAS exceeds at least two of three thresholds at the financial year-end: EUR 5 million balance-sheet total, EUR 10 million net turnover, and 50 average employees. Additional mandatory appointment rules apply to certain parent companies and companies controlling or controlled by qualifying groups, and may arise from specific regulated activities or shareholder requests.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under the French Accounting Standards Authority rules (ANC), with IFRS permitted or required in limited circumstances. French statutory annual accounts are generally prepared under French GAAP.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No standalone annual UBO confirmation is required in France. The company should conduct an annual review of ownership and control, update the beneficial-owner filing within 30 days of a relevant change, and update the share-transfer register, shareholders' register, and securities account records when shares are transferred. SAS share transfers are generally subject to registration formalities and transfer tax.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of shareholders or securities accounts and register of securities movements
Register of shareholder decisions and signed minutes
Corporate decision records and applicable directors' or officers' appointment and delegation records
Annual accounts, management reports, auditor reports where applicable, and supporting filing evidence

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: Approximately USD 650-1,950 per year, depending on city, mail handling, domiciliation services, and administrative support.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-12,000 for a small, non-complex SAS requiring a statutory audit; materially higher for international groups, inventory-intensive trading, or complex related-party transactions.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 15% reduced rate on first €42,500 for SMEs; R&D tax credit up to 30%; patent box regime for qualifying IP income

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065 (Déclaration de résultat) via impots.gouv.fr electronic filing portal

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust for transfer pricing and treaty relief
Pay electronically; claim foreign tax credits

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing €150 minimum to €75,000 maximum plus 0.5% per month of tax due (max 5%); interest 0.2% per month

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Apply for TRC (Certificat de Résidence Fiscale) via impots.gouv.fr; submit beneficial ownership certificate and DTA documentation

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Demonstrate real economic activity; report cross-border arrangements under DAC6

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to 500% of evaded tax plus 5 years imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability, disqualification, restitution orders

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €7.5 million or 5% of group turnover
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal fines and possible imprisonment for willful misconduct

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Company dissolution, fines up to €1.5 million
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal liability for damages and criminal sanctions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file STRs or comply with KYC
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million plus imprisonment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal liability and office disqualification
